subject: Artificial Intelligence
chapters: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms

questions.text: Define Artificial Intelligence. Explain the Turing Test and Chinese Room Argument. Explain Rational Agents and the PEAS (Performance Measure, Environment, Actuators, Sensors) framework for: (a) Automated Taxi Driver, and (b) Medical Diagnosis System.

Explain Environment Types in AI: Fully Observable vs Partially Observable, Deterministic vs Stochastic, Episodic vs Sequential, Static vs Dynamic, Discrete vs Continuous, and Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent. Classify Agent Architectures: Simple Reflex, Model-Based, Goal-Based, and Utility-Based agents.
Explain the concept of Agentic AI and how it differs from traditional AI systems. Discuss the interdisciplinary foundation of AI spanning Computer Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, and Philosophy.

Compare Uninformed Search Algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS), Depth-First Search (DFS), Uniform-Cost Search (UCS / Dijkstra), and Iterative Deepening DFS (IDDFS) in terms of Completeness, Time Complexity, Space Complexity, and Optimality.

Explain ^*$ Search Algorithm ((n) = g(n) + h(n)$). Define Admissible Heuristic ((n) \le h^*(n)$) and Consistent (Monotonic) Heuristic ((n) \le c(n, a, n') + h(n') $). Prove that Tree-search ^*$ is optimal with an admissible heuristic.
Solve the 8-Puzzle Problem from initial state to goal state using ^*$ search with: (1) Misplaced Tiles heuristic (n)$, and (2) Manhattan Distance heuristic (n)$. Why is $ dominant over 0

Explain Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP). Formalize the Map Coloring Problem (Australia map with 7 regions using 3 colors Red, Green, Blue) as a CSP. Explain Backtracking Search with MRV (Minimum Remaining Values), Degree heuristic, and Forward Checking / AC-3 algorithm.

Explain the Minimax Algorithm for two-player zero-sum games. Trace the Minimax algorithm and Alpha-Beta Pruning on a given 4-ply game tree. State the conditions for $lphahBccutoff and $ etahBccutoff ($lpha \ge  eta$).

Explain Local Search Algorithms: Hill Climbing (Steepest Ascent) and Simulated Annealing. How does Simulated Annealing escape local maxima using the Boltzmann probability distribution ( = e^{\Delta E / T}$)?
Explain Genetic Algorithms (GA) for optimization. Explain the basic operators: Selection (Roulette Wheel, Tournament), Crossover (Single-point, Two-point), and Mutation with an example.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Explain Knowledge Representation techniques: Semantic Networks, Frames, Conceptual Dependency, and Knowledge Graphs with examples.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Convert the following sentences into First-Order Predicate Logic (FOPL) and prove by Resolution Refutation: (a) Marcus was a man, (b) Marcus was a Pompeian, (c) All Pompeians were Romans, (d) Caesar was a ruler, (e) All Romans either loved Caesar or hated him, (f) Everyone loves someone, (g) People only try to assassinate rulers they hate, (h) Marcus tried to assassinate Caesar. Prove: Did Marcus hate Caesar?

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text:
Explain Probabilistic Reasoning and Bayesian Networks (Belief Networks). State Bayes' Theorem. Given prior probabilities (D) = 0.01$, and test accuracies (T^+|D) = 0.98$, (T^+|
eg D) = 0.05$, find the posterior probability (D|T^+)$ that a patient has the disease given a positive test result.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Explain Fuzzy Logic and Fuzzy Inference Systems (Mamdani vs Sugeno models). Define Membership Functions (Triangular, Trapezoidal, Gaussian) and explain Fuzzification, Fuzzy Rule Evaluation, and Defuzzification (Centroid / Center of Gravity method).
Explain the Four Pillars of Machine Learning (Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability & Statistics, Optimization). Differentiate between Generative vs Discriminative models with examples.
Explain Overfitting, Underfitting, Bias-Variance Tradeoff, and Cross-Validation. How do L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) Regularization prevent overfitting?

Explain Decision Tree induction using ID3 / C4.5 algorithm. Define Entropy (S) = -\sum p_i \log_2 p_i$ and Information Gain (S, A) = H(S) - \sum  rac{|S_v|}{|S|} H(S_v)$. Given a training dataset with 14 instances, calculate Information Gain for a split attribute.

Explain Support Vector Machines (SVM). Explain Maximum Margin Hyperplane, Support Vectors, Slack Variables for soft-margin classification, and the Kernel Trick (Linear, Polynomial, RBF kernels) for non-linearly separable data.

Explain Unsupervised Learning with t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) for high-dimensional data visualization. Explain Reinforcement Learning framework (Agent, Environment, State, Action, Reward, Q-Learning algorithm).
Explain Model Evaluation Metrics: Confusion Matrix, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Specificity, ROC Curve, and AUC (Area Under Curve).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Explain the Artificial Neuron (Perceptron) model. Derive the Perceptron Learning Rule. Explain why a Single-Layer Perceptron cannot solve the non-linear XOR problem (Linear Separability problem).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). Derive the Error Backpropagation Algorithm using the chain rule of calculus for weight updates with Sigmoid activation function (z) =  rac{1}{1+e^{-z}}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Activation Functions in Neural Networks: Sigmoid, Hyperbolic Tangent ($	anh$), ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), Leaky ReLU, and Softmax. Explain the Vanishing Gradient Problem.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Explain Deep Learning architectures: (a) Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN: Convolution, Pooling, Fully Connected layers), (b) Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN & LSTM for sequential data), and (c) Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN: Generator vs Discriminator).

Explain the Architecture and Characteristics of Expert Systems (Knowledge Base, Inference Engine: Forward vs Backward Chaining, Explanation Facility, User Interface). Explain the MYCIN or DENDRAL expert system.

Explain Natural Language Processing (NLP) levels of analysis: Phonological, Morphological, Syntactic (Parsing), Semantic, Pragmatic, and Discourse processing. Discuss NLP challenges (Ambiguity) and modern transformer-based LLMs.
Explain the role of AI in Computer Vision (Image Segmentation, Object Detection: YOLO) and Autonomous Robotics.
Explain Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) models and Self-Attention / Transformer architecture.
Explain Federated Learning (Privacy-preserving distributed training) and Edge AI (On-device machine learning inference).
Discuss Ethics in AI, AI Bias, Explainable AI (XAI), and Responsible AI deployment in Nepal's socio-economic context.
